Your first CSS rule

W3C CSS Snapshot 2026

CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) describes how HTML looks. HTML gives a paragraph its role on the page; CSS can change its color, spacing, and position. This lesson uses the HTML document structure you already built.

Open interactive lesson

Read one CSS rule

A rule selects HTML elements and lists what to change. Here p is the selector, so the rule applies to paragraph elements. The braces hold declarations. In color: teal, color is the property you change, and teal is the value you give it. A semicolon ends the declaration.

How to try it Save this example as a new .html file, then open it in your browser. After a change, save and reload.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Read one CSS rule</title>
  <style>
    p { color: teal; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
<p class="notice">Your order is ready.</p>
<p>Your package is on the way.</p>
</body>
</html>

What to expect Both paragraphs are teal. Change teal to purple and reload to see both change.

Where does <style> go?

The previous example puts a <style> element in <head>. The browser reads its CSS when it opens that HTML file. This is convenient for a small example you can copy into one file.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <title>CSS in the head</title>
    <style>
      p { color: teal; }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <p>Registration is open.</p>
  </body>
</html>

Link a separate CSS file

A stylesheet can live in its own .css file. In head, rel="stylesheet" tells the browser what the link is for, and href gives the file location. With both files in the same folder, the file name is enough.

How to try it Save the rule below in style.css beside the previous .html file. Remove its <style> block. In its place, inside <head>, write <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">. Save both files and reload.

p { color: purple; }

What to expect The browser reads style.css and makes the paragraphs purple.

If the result differs If the text stays unchanged, check that the link and file use exactly the same name and that both files are saved in the same folder.
